183992:
TESTIMONY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
IN OPPOSITION TO
L.D. 552
"An Act to Create an Outfitter License for Owners and Operators of Hunting, Fishing and
Recreational Businesses That Are Not Maine Guides"
Presented by: Senator GUERIN of Penobscot.
DATE OF HEARING: Monday, February 24, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Dan Scott, Colonel of the Maine Warden Service speaking on behalf of Maine Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, in opposition to L.D. 552.
This bill changes the legal definition of a Guide, creates a definition of an Outfitter and
establishes a new Outfitter license. The bill would change the definition of a guide significantly, which the Department feels is problematic. Currently, a guide is defined as anyone who receives any form of payment for accompanying or assisting a person in the fields or forests or on the waters or ice in Maine. The
bill proposes to remove the receipt of payment from the definition of a guide. This would mean, for example, that when a person takes a friend fishing or hunting it would be considered guiding
and would require a Guide license. In addition, the bill also proposes that the term "when training
is essential for the safety of the activity" be added to the definition of a guide. This proposal would open a whole area of discussion as to what activities might require safety training.
The bill also proposes to create the definition of an Outfitter and establish a new Outfitter license. The Department feels that this would be a burden on business owners and sees no good reason to
do so. I would be glad to answer any questions at this time or during the work session.

Testimony in Opposition to LD 552
An Act to Create an Outfitter License for Owners and Operators of
Hunting, Fishing and Recreation Businesses Who Are Not Maine Guides
February 24, 2025
Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the committee, my name is James Cote and l am here today on
behalf of the Maine Professional Guides Association in opposition to LD 552. This legislation is nearly identical to that of LD 1599 which was proposed in the previous Legislature. The Maine
Professional Guides Association maintains the same concerns that we did at that time.
First, amending the definition of "guide" as proposed in LD 552 could have significant unintended consequences as it
could capture all kinds of people who today are not guides. We have had extensive discussions with stakeholders in recent
years about the statutory definition of "guide" and continue to maintain that the current definition is valid and valuableand captures those people participating in guiding activities appropriately. l\/|aine's guiding requirements continue to be
known worldwide as some of the most rigorous, and as a result, we produce some of the finest, most professional and
capable guides anywhere in the world.
Second, we are unsure what the benefit of creating an outfitter license would be, or why it needs to be created. The
current definition of guide already captures activities where guide training and education is necessary, and where it is appropriate to regulate these activities. Creating this new license would be 1) duplicative in many case, and 2) create an additional, unwarranted layer of fees and requirements that could unintentionally apply to businesses from Maine and afar. While "outfitters" may be a regulated terms in places like western states, it is not interchangeable here in Maine under our current regulatory structure.
For these reasons, we urge you to oppose this legislation as the previous Legislature did. Thank you for your consideration
and l would be pleased to answer any questions or follow up with additional information as requested.

Stacey K. Guerin Senator, District 4

THE MAINE SENATE
l32nd Legislature

3 State House Station Augusta, Maine 04333

L.D. 552, "An Act to Create an Outfitter License for Owners and Operators of Hunting, Fishing and Recreation Businesses Who Are Not Maine Guides"
Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Monday, February 24, 2025

Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife:
I am Senator Stacey Guerin and I am here to present a bill I put in "By Request," L.D. 552, "An
Act to Create an Outfitter License for Owners and Operators of Hunting, Fishing and Recreation
Businesses Who Are Not Maine Guides."
This bill would create an outfitter license for people who own or operate businesses related to
hunting, fishing, or recreation but are not registered as Maine guides. This bill forms a regulatory path for businesses that play an important role in outdoor tourism in Maine, offering services
such as providing equipment, access, or other support for outdoor activities.
While outdoor recreation is important to Maine's economy, not all businesses need to be licensed as guides. This bill recognizes that distinction and provides a licensing system for businesses offering services such as equipment and access to activities.
The bill also includes a background check requirement for outfitters to help ensure safety and
trustworthiness. By establishing the outfitter license, the bill aims to create a clearer system for
outdoor businesses that don't need to be fully licensed guides but still contribute to the recreation and tourism economy.
Thank you for your time.
